papers.what_it_is: A theory-and-simulation paper that studies how hardware noise changes the overparametrization of quantum neural networks through the rank and eigenvalues of the quantum Fisher information matrix, with proofs for global depolarizing noise and for local depolarizing plus unital Pauli noise.

existing.anchor: Abstract, p.1; Section V, p.13; Section VI, pp.13-14
quotes: Finally, our results imply that current QNN capacity measures are ill-defined when hardware noise is present.

Let us briefly discuss the implications of the previous results for the capacity measures of Refs. [27, 28]. In particular, we have seen that both these measures are related to the maximum rank of the quantum or classical Fisher information matrix.
We find that measures based on the QFIM rank can be misleading when noise is taken into account.
The critical issue here is that the rank of the QFIM is a discrete number that depends on the number of strictly non-zero eigenvalues of the QFIM, but not on their magnitude.
